trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court at Bangalore, M.C.No.77/2016
case_name: Smt Chandrika M S vs Sri Aparajit I V

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Chandrika M.S., wife, assistant teacher

facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The respondent filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights which was dismissed by the trial court. The petitioner has appealed against this order.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: It is agreed that the appellant and the respondent do not get along well and there was irretrievable break down of marriage and they have been living separately from February 2013 and there are no chances of reunion.

legal_principles.principle: A settlement arrived at between the parties can be a valid basis for granting divorce.
legal_principles.held: In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties, husband has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards permanent alimony/maintenance to the wife in full and final settlement of all her claims.

outcome.final_order: The appeals are allowed and the impugned judgment is set aside.

use_for_drafting: settling property disputes in a divorce case
